subject: Clarify: incident notification timelines, subprocessors & DPA language
messages:
From: Elaine Klein <elaine.klein@paxford.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@paxford.com>, legal@paxford.com
Date: Wed, 05 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA: incident notification timelines + subprocessors

Marissa —

Thanks for the earlier conversation. Paxford is reviewing the draft DPA and we have a couple of sticking points before procurement will move forward. The items that need explicit confirmation are:

- Incident notification timeline and scope: we need explicit language that Redwood will notify Paxford within 24 hours of becoming aware of any security incident that reasonably may have resulted in unauthorized access to Paxford data (please include the expected initial contents of that notice).
- Cooperation: commitment to provide root cause analysis and remediation plans within 30 days for incidents impacting personal data and continued updates until closure.
- Subprocessors: a current inventory and a process for prior notice or objection when adding a new subprocessor that might involve cross-border transfers.
- Data transfers: confirmation that transfers from EU customer data are protected by SCCs or equivalent and that Redwood will provide copies on request.

I have attached a redline of the DPA with marked clauses (Paxford_DPA_redline_20251105.pdf) and a requested clause template for notifications. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the 24-hour initial notice and the 30-day root-cause window, or propose commercial/legal guardrails if you cannot?

If you prefer, we can set a quick call with Paxford procurement/infosec (Alex + legal) this week.

Thanks,
Elaine Klein
Head of Privacy & Contracts
Paxford Financial

[attachment: Paxford_DPA_redline_20251105.pdf (PDF)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Klein <elaine.klein@paxford.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 05 Nov 2025 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA: incident notification timelines + subprocessors

Elaine —

Appreciate the clear asks and the redline. Looping in Rishi (legal) and Vivek (security) to confirm technical feasibility and proposed contract language.

High-level response before we dig in:
- We generally commit to "prompt" notification and can support a tiered timeline. 24 hours for confirmed/severe unauthorized-access incidents is reasonable where we have enough signal to notify (e.g., confirmed system compromise). For suspected incidents where investigation is needed, our typical practice is to provide an initial notification within 48–72 hours indicating we are investigating, with an update as soon as material new info is known.
- Root-cause analysis delivery within 30 days is often feasible for many incidents; exceptional cases (multi-team forensic investigations) may require an extension with interim status updates.
- We maintain a real-time subprocessor inventory and will provide the current list and a process for notices. We can tolerate a 10-business-day review/objection period for new subprocessors if Paxford wants a chance to object to specific providers handling regulated data.
- Transfers: we use SCCs where applicable and can provide proof on request; for customers on Dedicated/Private deployments we can limit transfers per contractual controls.

Rishi/Vivek — can you review the attached Paxford redline and produce a minimal Redwood counter that preserves our operational constraints but gives Paxford visibility? I sketched a proposed notification paragraph below — feel free to redline.

Proposed initial-notice language (draft):
"Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide Customer with written notice of any security incident affecting Customer Data no later than 24 hours after Redwood confirms a high-severity incident. For incidents that require additional investigation to confirm scope, Redwood will provide preliminary notice within 48–72 hours summarizing the known facts and next steps, and will follow up with timely updates. Redwood will provide a root cause analysis and remediation plan within 30 days for incidents impacting Personal Data, subject to extension where forensic investigation requires additional time; Redwood will provide interim status reports during such an extension."

Thoughts?

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

[forwarded attachment: subprocessor_inventory_2025-11-05.csv]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 06 Nov 2025 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA: incident notification timelines + subprocessors

Team —

Reviewed Paxford's redline. Key legal positions to defend and trade-offs to propose:

1) 24-hour flat requirement for "becoming aware" is operationally risky. We should instead accept: 24 hours for confirmed high-severity incidents; 48–72 hours for suspected incidents where further triage is required. That allows for noise and transient alerts.

2) Root-cause in 30 days: we can commit to reasonable best efforts to deliver RCA and remediation plan within 30 days for incidents impacting personal data, with an explicit carve-out allowing extension when third-party forensics or law enforcement coordination is necessary. Must avoid hard contractual SLA that creates liability for ongoing investigations.

3) Subprocessor objection period: 10 business days to raise objections is acceptable. We cannot guarantee pausing a subprocessor onboarding indefinitely; propose an "opt-out" right limited to specified categories of high-risk subprocessors and a mutual escalation path.

4) Cross-border transfers: confirm SCCs; provide statement of transfer mechanisms in the DPA and agree to provide documentation on request.

I drafted language that preserves Paxford's need for speed but protects Redwood from unrealistic SLAs. See attached "incident-notification-playbook-Redwood.docx" with suggested contractual text.

Rishi
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

[attachment: incident-notification-playbook-Redwood.docx]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 07 Nov 2025 11:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA: incident notification timelines + subprocessors

Marissa/Rishi —

From an operations and IR perspective:

- 24 hours for confirmed high-severity incidents: doable if we have clear internal definitions and a rapid detection pipeline. We should include a short definition of "high-severity" in contract or an appendix (e.g., confirmed exfiltration, unauthorized access to unencrypted customer data, production compromise affecting availability/security).
- For suspected incidents we must retain 48–72 hours to validate and avoid false positives.
- RCA within 30 days: fine in most cases; will require coordination with our cloud provider and any engaged forensic vendor. We propose contract language that allows an additional 30-day extension with written notice to customer if third-party forensics are required.
- Subprocessors: current inventory attached. We can offer 10-business-day notice and an objection window limited to subprocessors that will have access to plaintext customer data or are outside standard EU transfer protections.

I'll add an operational appendix outlining initial notice contents (time detected, systems affected, initial scope, immediate mitigations, contact for updates). That appendix can be referenced in the DPA so that Paxford sees the information they will receive in the first notice.

-Vivek
Head of Security Operations

[attachment: subprocessor_inventory_2025-11-05.csv]

From: Elaine Klein <elaine.klein@paxford.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@paxford.com>, legal@paxford.com
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA: incident notification timelines + subprocessors

Marissa —

Thanks for the quick internal review and the playbook — that helps a lot. Paxford legal is prepared to accept a tiered timeline as you described with the following adjustments we would like to see reflected in the DPA:

- Section X.1 (Notification): "For high-severity incidents involving confirmed unauthorized access to Customer Data, Redwood shall provide initial written notice no later than 24 hours after Redwood confirms such an incident. For incidents where confirmation requires additional investigation, Redwood shall provide preliminary notice within 48–72 hours of becoming aware and continue to provide updates until the incident is closed."
- Section X.2 (RCA): "Redwood shall provide a root cause analysis and remediation plan within 30 calendar days following notice of an incident impacting Personal Data, with the ability to extend by up to 30 additional days if Redwood demonstrates that third-party forensics or law enforcement coordination is required; Redwood shall provide interim status updates at least every 7 calendar days during any such extension."
- Subprocessors: Paxford accepts a 10-business-day objection window with the right to object only where the subprocessor will process Personal Data on Paxford's behalf in a manner that creates material additional risk; Redwood will provide a description of technical and organizational controls for any challenged subprocessor.

I've attached our final redline reflecting the above (Paxford_DPA_redline_20251111.pdf). If Redwood agrees, procurement will route the DPA for signature and we'll return a countersigned copy within 3–5 business days.

We prefer DocuSign for execution; please confirm who should receive the envelope.

Best,
Elaine

[attachment: Paxford_DPA_redline_20251111.pdf (PDF)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Klein <elaine.klein@paxford.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 Nov 2025 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA: incident notification timelines + subprocessors

Elaine —

This is all good news. Redwood accepts the tiered notification language and the RCA timeline with the limited extension and interim update cadence. We also accept the 10-business-day objection window on new subprocessors with the requested scope.

Please send the DocuSign envelope to contracts@redwood.ai (cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai). We'll get this routed on our side and expect to countersign within 2 business days of receipt.

I'll also attach the final incident-notification appendix referenced in our playbook for Paxford's records.

Thanks for working through this — looking forward to getting the DPA executed.

Marissa
Sr. Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
